demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.label: 01 / AI + IoT ENERGY SYSTEM
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.title: Demand Forecasting and Dynamic Pricing
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.intro: An intelligent energy system that connects real-time IoT monitoring with machine-learning forecasts to make transformer-load decisions more informed.
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.problem: Electricity demand can change quickly, making it difficult to anticipate transformer load and respond before overload becomes a risk. A useful solution needed to observe live conditions, forecast demand, and translate those predictions into practical pricing recommendations.
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.approach: The system combines ESP32-based monitoring, ThingSpeak data, an LSTM forecasting model, and a Streamlit interface. Forecasted demand is used to generate dynamic pricing recommendations that encourage more efficient energy usage.
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.contribution: I worked across the system, including IoT data collection, the LSTM forecasting workflow, data analysis, dashboard presentation, and the connection between predictions and pricing logic.
demand-forecasting-dynamic-pricing.outcome: The project brings machine learning, embedded systems, and energy decision-making into one practical workflow designed to improve energy efficiency and reduce overload pressure.

acta.label: 02 / HACKXTREME’26
acta.title: Acta — Meeting Application
acta.intro: A meeting assistant that transforms conversations into organised minutes, decisions, and actionable tasks so teams can focus on progress instead of paperwork.
acta.problem: Important meeting information is often scattered across notes and memory. Teams need a faster way to capture what was discussed, what was decided, and what should happen next without interrupting collaboration.
acta.approach: Acta listens to meeting content, interprets the discussion, and organises the output into structured minutes, decisions, and tasks. The product was shaped during a 24-hour hackathon around a simple goal: make meetings produce usable progress.
acta.contribution: I contributed to the product thinking, application development, AI and NLP workflow, and the process of turning the prototype into a clear and effective hackathon demonstration.
acta.outcome: Acta won first place at HackXtreme’26 at K. Ramakrishnan College of Engineering, validating the idea, execution, and presentation under a demanding 24-hour build window.

food-bridge.label: 03 / TECHHACKS 2.0
food-bridge.title: Food Bridge — Redistribution Platform
food-bridge.intro: A smart food redistribution platform that helps surplus food move quickly and responsibly from donors to the people and organisations that need it.
food-bridge.problem: Surplus food can go to waste when donors, NGOs, volunteers, and logistics partners do not have a simple way to coordinate. The challenge was to make food donation more visible, connected, and actionable.
food-bridge.approach: Food Bridge brings the main participants in the redistribution process together through one platform. It focuses on simplifying donation, coordinating support, and helping surplus food reach the right destination efficiently.
food-bridge.contribution: I contributed to the mobile application experience, Flutter and Dart implementation, API integration, and the use of intelligent ideas to make the redistribution workflow more practical.
food-bridge.outcome: Food Bridge secured second place at TechHacks 2.0, an international hackathon hosted by SRM Ramapuram at Genesys, Infocity.
